questions.text: Which sequence matches the regular design service phases described in SPP Document 202?

options.text: Schematic Design, Design Development, Contract Documents, Bidding/Negotiation, and Construction only
Project Definition, Schematic Design, Design Development, Contract Documents, Bidding/Negotiation, and Construction Phase
Pre-Design, Design, Build, Operate, and Post-Occupancy
Consultation, Site Selection, Space Management, Value Management, and Promotional Services

questions.rationale: SPP 202 lists Project Definition first, then Schematic Design, Design Development, Contract Document, Bidding/Negotiation, and Construction Phase services.

questions.text: In SPP 202 work-suspended-or-abandoned wording, once the architect has prepared the plans, specifications, and other building construction documents, that completed work is equivalent to what share of the architect's work?

options.text: 35% of the architect's work
85% of the architect's work
90% of the architect's work
100% of the architect's work

questions.rationale: SPP 202 states that when the detailed design and contract documents are prepared, that phase is equivalent to ninety percent of the architect's work in the abandonment context.

questions.text: Which project type belongs to SPP 202 Group 4 in the checked local source?

options.text: Airports, ports, hospitals, hotels, theaters, and similar complex facilities
Residences, small apartment houses, and townhouses
Built-in components, special fittings, screens, counters, and architectural interiors
Alterations, renovations, rehabilitations, retrofit, and expansion to existing Groups 1 to 5 buildings

questions.rationale: The checked SPP 202 source identifies Group 4 as residences, small apartment houses, and townhouses.

questions.text: Which work belongs to SPP 202 Group 9 in the checked local source?

options.text: New residences and townhouses
Projects involving extensive built-in detail, special fittings, or architectural interiors
Alterations, renovations, rehabilitations, retrofit, and expansion/additions to existing Groups 1 to 5 buildings
Technical opinions, advice, clarifications, or explanations on architectural works

questions.rationale: The checked SPP 202 source defines Group 9 as alterations, renovations, rehabilitations, retrofit, and expansion/additions to existing buildings belonging to Groups 1 to 5.

questions.text: What characterizes SPP 202 Group 8 in the checked local source?

options.text: Projects involving extensive detail such as built-in components, equipment, special fittings, screens, counters, interiors, and development planning/design
Small apartment houses and townhouses
Projects where the same drawings are reused for repetitive similar buildings
Opinions and advice on technical matters pertaining to architectural works

questions.rationale: The checked SPP 202 source describes Group 8 as projects involving extensive detail, including built-in elements, equipment, special fittings, screens, counters, architectural interiors, and development planning/design.

questions.text: Under SPP 202, how many sets of construction drawings and technical specifications does the architect submit to the Owner for building permit purposes?

options.text: Five sets
Six sets
Seven sets
Eight sets

questions.rationale: SPP 202 states that the architect submits seven sets of all construction drawings and technical specifications for building permit purposes.

questions.text: Under SPP 202 owner responsibilities, through whom should the Owner issue orders to the General Contractor?

options.text: Directly to the General Contractor
Through the local government building official
Through the Architect
Through the supplier with the largest contract amount

questions.rationale: The checked SPP 202 owner-responsibility text says the Owner should issue orders to the General Contractor only through the Architect.

questions.text: Under SPP 202, per diem plus travel and living expenses become chargeable when services are required beyond what radial distance from the architect's established office?

options.text: 25.0 kilometers
50.0 kilometers
75.0 kilometers
100.0 kilometers

questions.rationale: SPP 202 uses beyond 50.0 kilometers, measured as air, straight-line, or radial distance from the architect's established office.

questions.text: Under SPP 202, what happens to the fee for remaining works when construction suspension exceeds six months?

options.text: It remains unchanged
It is reduced to the direct personnel expense only
It is doubled for the remaining works
It is converted automatically to a lump-sum government-project fee

questions.rationale: SPP 202 states that when construction suspension exceeds six months, the fee for the remaining works shall be doubled.

questions.text: Under SPP 202, is regular construction-phase service the same as continuous eight-hour on-site supervision?

options.text: Yes; SPP 202 requires the architect to supervise continuously for eight hours each day
No; SPP 202 includes periodic site visits, and full-time eight-hour supervision is a separate service when required
Yes; continuous supervision replaces the need for certificates for payment
No; SPP 202 has no construction-phase role for the architect

questions.rationale: SPP 202 states that the architect makes periodic site visits and is not required to make exhaustive or continuous eight-hour on-site supervision; full-time supervision is covered separately when required.
